title: Local with opus plausible?
author: advator
selftext:
Using a local LLM as a “worker” for Blender/Unreal, with Claude Opus as the brain?

I’m thinking about building a setup where a local LLM runs on my RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB VRAM) and handles most of the repetitive 3D work through MCP.

Something like:

Local Qwen 7B/8B

→ Blender MCP

→ Unreal MCP

→ Blender / Unreal

The local model would handle things like:

\- Creating and modifying geometry

\- Blender Python

\- Materials and lighting

\- Setting up actors

\- Basic Blueprints

\- Moving/scaling/duplicating objects

\- Import/export

\- Repetitive scene construction

Then, for more complex tasks, it could call Claude Opus 5.5.

For example:

"Create a new house similar to the existing houses, but redesign the layout to create a more interesting horror gameplay flow."

The local model could recognize that this requires more reasoning and ask Opus for a high-level solution. Opus would provide the plan, and the local model would execute it through Blender/Unreal MCP.

The main reason I’m interested in this isn't to replace Claude. It’s to save Opus tokens.

Why use Opus to generate hundreds of simple Blender/Unreal tool calls when a local model can handle those cheaply and quickly?

Ideally:

Local model = fast 3D worker

Opus = senior/creative reasoning when needed

Has anyone built something similar?

I’m particularly interested in whether a 7B/8B model is actually good enough at Blender + Unreal MCP for this kind of workflow, and how people would implement the handoff between the local model and Claude.

Is this plausible?

comments.author: Shin-Zantesu
comments.body: The best thing you can do is try it. I personally stopped using the local model very quickly, too much computer resources and it requires a lot of setup and it's not great at judging its results. Besides, who said you need Opus? Sonnet is cheaper. A Muse Code subscription gives you the contributor version of muse spark 1.3, which is great and very generous with the usage (especially for what you have to do)

comments.author: sunnystormy64
comments.body:
I've done this already and am cooking up a better solution.

Here are the challenges:

1. Your cloud "supervisor" will burn through tokens.

2. Your local model will lose access to its supervisor for guidance quicker than you'd like.

The solution:

1. You need to research better fine-tunes for local models on HuggingFace.

The Future:

\-Before the end of 2027 we should have cloud-level intelligence that can fit on consumer GPUs at various quantizations. In my view, that's the "official" burst of the AI bubble, and why tech companies want to slow down AI progress. They can't milk us through subscriptions if democracy wins.

My recommendation (given your constraints) is, again, to look for fine-tunes on HF that apply to your hardware setup. Otherwise, find a subscription plan to carry you into 2027 knowing that it won't be permanent. You have to reconcile personal philosophy with "getting it done". Just my two cents.

Good luck!

comments.author: MattMaxBuilds
comments.body:
8B won’t get you much besides populating dialog trees and other low-risk work. It’ll probably botch anything meaningfully agentic.

A lot of the Chinese models are benchmaxxed too. They look great on leaderboards and then fall apart once you put them in a real workflow.

Unless you have ~96GB VRAM laying around, I wouldn’t offload much meaningful work to local models. I’m not counting heavily quantized stuff either. FP16/BF16 or bust.
